free-state-of-brunswick.t: Republican successor of the Duchy of Brunswick, remembered for giving Adolf Hitler German citizenship in 1932.
free-state-of-brunswick.o: Duke Ernest Augustus abdicated on 8 November 1918, and a socialist republic was proclaimed in Brunswick. After a period of councils and unrest, a constitution was adopted in 1922, making Brunswick a parliamentary free state.
free-state-of-brunswick.r: Brunswick had industry, canning and the Büssing vehicle works, and its politics were polarised between Social Democrats and the right. From 1930 the Nazis shared government, and in February 1932 the Nazi interior minister Dietrich Klagges appointed Adolf Hitler to a nominal post in the state's Berlin legation, which made the stateless Hitler a German citizen and allowed him to run for president.
free-state-of-brunswick.e: After 1945 Brunswick was in the British zone. In November 1946 it was merged with Hanover, [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] and [[s:principality-of-schaumburg-lippe|Schaumburg-Lippe]] into the new state of Lower Saxony.

federation-of-south-arabia.t: Britain's last attempt to build a friendly state around Aden, which collapsed under nationalist insurgency in 1967.
federation-of-south-arabia.o: In April 1962 the [[s:federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south|Federation of Arab Emirates of the South]] was renamed the Federation of [[e:south-arabia|South Arabia]]. In January 1963 the [[s:colony-of-aden|Colony of Aden]] joined as the [[s:state-of-aden|State of Aden]], despite opposition from Aden's trade unions and nationalists, and more [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] states joined in the following years.
federation-of-south-arabia.r: The federation was ruled by sultans, [[e:emir|emirs]] and sheikhs with British advisers, and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] kept its military base at Aden. In December 1963 a grenade attack on the High Commissioner at Aden airport led to a state of emergency. Two rival movements, the National Liberation Front and FLOSY, fought the British and each other in Aden and the Radfan mountains.
federation-of-south-arabia.e: In 1966 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] announced it would leave without a defence agreement. In 1967 the federal army and states collapsed as the National Liberation Front took over; [[e:britain|Britain]] withdrew on 29 November 1967 and [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]] became independent.

free-imperial-city-of-nordlingen.t: Walled Swabian imperial city inside the Ries meteorite crater, known for its Whitsun fair and the two battles of Nördlingen in the Thirty Years War.
free-imperial-city-of-nordlingen.o: A royal estate at Nördlingen in the Ries basin, an ancient meteorite crater, passed to the [[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-regensburg|Regensburg]] and back to the Hohenstaufen. In 1215 Emperor [[e:frederick-ii|Frederick II]] recognised it as an imperial city, and its growth was helped by its position on the roads between Franconia, Swabia and Bavaria.
free-imperial-city-of-nordlingen.r: A council dominated by merchants ruled the city. Its Whitsun fair was one of the leading markets of southern [[e:germany|Germany]], and cloth, leather and [[e:fur-trade|furs]] were its main trades. Nördlingen adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in the 1520s. The great hall church of St. Georg, with its tall tower known as the Daniel, and an intact ring of walls testify to its wealth.
free-imperial-city-of-nordlingen.e: The city suffered in the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years War]], when imperial and Spanish troops won the first Battle of Nördlingen in 1634 and French forces fought there again in 1645. It lost its freedom in 1803 to the [[s:electorate-of-bavaria|Electorate of Bavaria]].

former-yan.t: The Murong Xianbei kingdom that rose in Liaoning and briefly ruled the North China Plain from Ye, until the Former Qin conquered it in 370.
former-yan.o: The Murong [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] settled in western Liaoning in the 3rd century and adopted farming and Chinese administration under Murong Hui. His son Murong [[s:state-of-huang|Huang]] declared himself King of Yan in 337, moving the capital to Longcheng (Chaoyang) in 342. He destroyed the [[s:yuwen-xianbei|Yuwen Xianbei]] in 344 and sacked the [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] capital in 342.
former-yan.r: Former Yan combined [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] cavalry with Chinese officials and farmers resettled from the war-torn plain. After [[s:later-zhao|Later Zhao]] collapsed, Murong Jun conquered the north-east plain, captured Ran Min in 352, proclaimed himself emperor and moved the capital to Ye in 357. The regent Murong Ke was a capable administrator and general.
former-yan.e: After Murong Ke died, court jealousy drove out the talented general Murong Chui, who had defeated Huan Wen at Fangtou in 369; he fled to [[s:former-qin|Former Qin]]. In 370 the [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] chancellor Wang Meng took Ye and captured the emperor Murong Wei. Murong princes later founded [[s:later-yan|Later Yan]], [[s:western-yan|Western Yan]] and [[s:southern-yan|Southern Yan]].

free-imperial-city-of-gengenbach.t: A small Black Forest imperial city in the Kinzig valley that grew around a Benedictine abbey and kept its freedom until 1803.
free-imperial-city-of-gengenbach.o: Gengenbach grew around a Benedictine abbey founded in the 8th century. The town received its rights under the Hohenstaufen and in the 14th century became a free imperial city, recognised by [[e:charles-iv|Charles IV]] in 1360. With [[s:free-imperial-city-of-zell-am-harmersbach|Zell am Harmersbach]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-offenburg|Offenburg]] it lay within the imperial bailiwick of the Ortenau, which emperors often pledged to neighbouring princes.
free-imperial-city-of-gengenbach.r: A council of [[e:burghers|burghers]] governed the town, whose economy rested on wine, [[e:timber|timber]], crafts and traffic along the Kinzig valley route through the Black Forest. Relations with the abbey were often tense. Gengenbach briefly accepted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] but returned to [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]]. French troops burned it in 1689 during the Nine Years' War, and it was rebuilt in Baroque style.
free-imperial-city-of-gengenbach.e: In 1803 the mediatisation gave Gengenbach and its neighbours to Baden, which became the [[s:grand-duchy-of-baden|Grand Duchy of Baden]] in 1806. Its half-timbered old town, walls and town hall survive.

federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia.t: Present-day Ethiopia, a federation of ethnically defined regions and Africa's second most populous country, shaped by rapid growth and civil conflict.
federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia.o: The constitution adopted in December 1994 replaced the [[s:transitional-government-of-ethiopia|Transitional Government of Ethiopia]], and after elections the Federal Democratic Republic of [[e:ethiopia|Ethiopia]] was proclaimed in August 1995. Meles Zenawi of the EPRDF became prime minister, holding power until his death in 2012.
federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia.r: The constitution created a federation of ethnically based regional states, each with the right to self-determination. Under the EPRDF [[e:ethiopia|Ethiopia]] achieved rapid economic growth through state-led investment in roads, dams and industry, but the party dominated politics and suppressed opposition. A war with [[s:state-of-eritrea|Eritrea]] from 1998 to 2000 and the disputed elections of 2005 marked its early years.
federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia.e: Protests brought Abiy Ahmed to power in 2018; he made peace with [[s:state-of-eritrea|Eritrea]] and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2019. The [[s:tigray|Tigray]] war of 2020 to 2022, ended by the Pretoria agreement, killed hundreds of thousands. [[e:ethiopia|Ethiopia]] remains a federal republic with [[e:addis-ababa|Addis Ababa]] as capital.

free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck.t: The Queen of the Hanse, a Baltic port whose law and merchants shaped dozens of towns from Tallinn to Gdańsk and which stayed a free state until 1937.
free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck.o: Henry the Lion refounded [[e:lubeck|Lübeck]] on the Trave in 1159 as a German port to the Baltic. After his fall the town came under the emperor, and in 1226 [[e:frederick-ii|Frederick II]] granted it the status of a free imperial city. Its merchants soon led the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanseatic League]], which held its diets in Lübeck.
free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck.r: A council of merchant families ruled the city, and [[e:lubeck|Lübeck]] law was adopted by about a hundred Baltic towns. Wealth came from trade in herring, salt, grain, [[e:fur-trade|furs]] and [[e:timber|timber]], visible in the Holstentor and St. Mary's Church. Lübeck turned Lutheran in 1530, and under the mayor Jürgen Wullenwever it waged the disastrous Count's Feud against [[e:denmark|Denmark]] in 1534 to 1536.
free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck.e: As the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanse]] faded [[e:lubeck|Lübeck]] declined. It was annexed by [[e:france|France]] from 1811 to 1813, then joined the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]] and [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] as a city-state. The Greater [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-hamburg|Hamburg]] Act of 1937 merged it into [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]]. Its old town is a World Heritage Site.

free-state-of-bavaria.t: Bavaria as a republic, from the 1918 revolution through the Nazi era to a prosperous and self-confident state of modern Germany.
free-state-of-bavaria.o: On 7 November 1918 the Independent Socialist Kurt Eisner proclaimed the Free State of Bavaria in Munich, ending the Wittelsbach monarchy. Eisner was assassinated in February 1919, and a short-lived [[s:bavarian-soviet-republic|Bavarian Soviet Republic]] was crushed that spring. The Bamberg constitution of 1919 established Bavaria as a parliamentary free state.
free-state-of-bavaria.r: Inter-war Bavaria became a conservative stronghold and refuge of the extreme right, where Hitler's Beer Hall Putsch failed in 1923. After 1933 the Nazis took control and Munich became the capital of the movement. After 1945 Bavaria was in the American zone; its 1946 constitution created a state long dominated by the Christian Social Union, which built a high-technology economy.
free-state-of-bavaria.e: Bavaria joined the [[s:federal-republic-of-germany|Federal Republic of Germany]] in 1949, though its Landtag rejected the Basic Law while accepting its validity. It remains one of [[e:germany|Germany's]] sixteen states, with Munich as capital.

french-fourth-republic.t: France's post-war parliamentary republic, unstable in government but launching European integration and rapid economic growth before collapsing over Algeria.
french-fourth-republic.o: After the [[s:provisional-government-of-the-french-republic|Provisional Government of the French Republic]], voters approved a new constitution in October 1946. It created a strong National Assembly and a weak president; Vincent Auriol was the first. The colonies were reorganised as the [[e:french-union|French Union]].
french-fourth-republic.r: Coalitions changed constantly, with more than twenty governments in twelve years. Yet economic modernisation was rapid, guided by Jean Monnet's planning. Robert Schuman proposed the European [[e:coal|Coal]] and [[e:steel|Steel]] Community in 1950, and [[e:france|France]] signed the Treaty of [[e:rome|Rome]] in 1957. Defeat at [[e:battle-of-dien-bien-phu|Dien Bien Phu]] ended the [[e:indochina|Indochina]] war in 1954, and Pierre Mendès France negotiated the withdrawal.
french-fourth-republic.e: The [[e:algerian-war|Algerian War]], begun in 1954, divided the nation. In May 1958 army officers and settlers seized power in [[e:algiers|Algiers]], and parliament called back [[e:charles-de-gaulle|Charles de Gaulle]], who drew up a new constitution creating the [[s:french-fifth-republic|French Fifth Republic]].

french-saint-barthelemy.t: Small, dry French island in the Leewards that passed through the hands of the Knights of Malta before France traded it to Sweden in 1784.
french-saint-barthelemy.o: French settlers from [[s:colony-of-saint-christopher|Saint Kitts]], sent by the governor Philippe de Longvilliers de Poincy, occupied [[s:saint-barthelemy-swedish|Saint-Barthélemy]] in 1648. In 1651 the island was included in the sale of French [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]] islands to the Knights Hospitaller. A Kalinago attack in 1656 wiped out the settlement, and it was repopulated only slowly, partly by settlers from [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]] and [[s:duchy-of-brittany|Brittany]].
french-saint-barthelemy.r: Lacking water and good soil, the island never became a plantation colony. Its small population of white smallholders lived by fishing, salt, livestock and modest [[e:cotton|cotton]] growing, with relatively few enslaved people. It was governed as a dependency of [[s:colony-of-guadeloupe|Guadeloupe]] or [[s:colony-of-saint-christopher|Saint Kitts]] rather than as a full colony, and its harbour, Le Carénage, was the only real settlement. The British occupied it briefly in the 18th century.
french-saint-barthelemy.e: In 1784 Louis XVI ceded the island to [[e:sweden|Sweden]] in exchange for trading rights in Gothenburg. The Swedes renamed the harbour Gustavia and made it a free port. [[e:france|France]] bought the island back in 1878, and it is now an overseas collectivity of France.

free-imperial-city-of-ulm.t: Danube imperial city of fustian weavers and merchants, builder of the minster with the world's tallest church spire and a leader of the Swabian League.
free-imperial-city-of-ulm.o: Ulm grew around a royal palace at the meeting of the Blau and the [[e:danube|Danube]], recorded from 854. It was a favoured Hohenstaufen town, and after their fall it was confirmed as an imperial city, its privileges renewed by Rudolf I in 1274.
free-imperial-city-of-ulm.r: The Schwörbrief of 1397 gave the [[e:guild|guilds]] a majority on the council, and the mayor swore an annual oath to the citizens. Fustian weaving and the [[e:danube|Danube]] trade made Ulm rich, and it acquired the largest territory of any imperial city after [[s:free-imperial-city-of-nuremberg|Nuremberg]]. Its citizens began the minster in 1377. Ulm led the Swabian city leagues and the Swabian League, and turned Protestant in 1530 to 1531.
free-imperial-city-of-ulm.e: Ulm lost its freedom to Bavaria in 1802 and passed to Württemberg in 1810; [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] defeated an Austrian army there in 1805. The minster spire was completed in 1890, and Albert Einstein was born in Ulm in 1879.

first-republic-of-armenia.t: The first modern Armenian state, born in 1918 amid war, genocide and famine, which survived two and a half years before Sovietisation.
first-republic-of-armenia.o: As the [[s:transcaucasian-democratic-federative-republic|Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic]] broke up, the Armenian National Council declared independence on 28 May 1918, just as Armenian forces halted an Ottoman offensive at Sardarabad. The Treaty of Batum in June 1918 left the new state a small territory around Erivan, crowded with refugees from the Armenian [[e:genocide|genocide]].
first-republic-of-armenia.r: The republic was governed by the Armenian Revolutionary Federation, with prime ministers Hovhannes Kajaznuni and Alexander Khatisian and a parliament elected by universal suffrage, including women. It faced famine, epidemics and border wars with [[s:georgia|Georgia]] and [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]]. After the Ottoman defeat it expanded to Kars, and the Treaty of Sevres in 1920 promised it much of eastern [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]].
first-republic-of-armenia.e: In autumn 1920 Turkish nationalist forces invaded, and in December 1920 the government ceded power to the Bolsheviks, creating the [[s:armenian-ssr|Armenian SSR]]. Its flag and declaration were revived by independent [[s:armenia|Armenia]] in 1991.

first-maldivian-republic.t: A short-lived republic that briefly replaced the Maldivian sultanate in 1953 under Mohamed Amin Didi.
first-maldivian-republic.o: Mohamed Amin Didi, a reforming politician and prime minister, led the [[s:republic-of-maldives|Maldives]] towards abolishing the sultanate after the throne fell vacant. A referendum approved a republic, which was proclaimed on 1 January 1953, with Amin Didi as president, while the islands remained a British [[e:protectorate|protectorate]].
first-maldivian-republic.r: Amin Didi pursued modernisation, promoting education, women's rights and the nationalisation of the fish export trade. These policies, together with food shortages and a ban on tobacco smoking, made his government unpopular.
first-maldivian-republic.e: While Amin Didi was abroad for medical treatment in 1953 he was overthrown; he died early in 1954 after an attack by a crowd. The republic was abolished and the [[s:sultanate-of-the-maldives|Sultanate of the Maldives]] was restored in 1954.

fadhli-sultanate.t: A tribal sultanate on the Abyan coast east of Aden, a member of the British-backed south Arabian federation until 1967.
fadhli-sultanate.o: The Fadhli tribe held the coastal plain of Abyan and the hills behind it. In the late 17th century, as the [[s:qasimid-state|Qasimid State]] lost its hold over the south, the Fadhli chiefs established an independent sultanate, with Shuqra on the coast as its chief town.
fadhli-sultanate.r: The sultans governed through tribal custom, controlling routes between Aden and the interior. In the 19th century they often raided the outskirts of [[s:aden-settlement|British Aden]] before signing a protection treaty with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], becoming part of the [[s:aden-protectorate|Aden Protectorate]]. From the 1940s the Abyan irrigation scheme turned the delta into a [[e:cotton|cotton]]-growing area, bringing new revenue. The sultanate joined the [[s:federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south|Federation of Arab Emirates of the South]] in 1959.
fadhli-sultanate.e: It was a member of the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]] until 1967, when the National Liberation Front took over the territory, abolished the sultanate and incorporated it into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.t: The Hyksos kings of Avaris, rulers of Levantine origin who governed northern Egypt for about a century.
fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.o: Around 1650 BCE rulers of Levantine descent, called [[e:hyksos|Hyksos]] from the Egyptian for 'rulers of foreign lands', took power at Avaris in the eastern Delta and captured Memphis, ending the [[s:middle-kingdom-of-egypt|Middle Kingdom of Egypt]]. Later Egyptian tradition portrayed this as an invasion, but it grew from a long-settled Canaanite population in the Delta.
fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.r: The [[e:hyksos|Hyksos]] adopted pharaonic titles and Egyptian administration while keeping Levantine customs at Avaris, where their great palaces and temples have been excavated. They worshipped Seth, identified with the storm god Baal, and traded widely with [[e:canaan|Canaan]] and [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]]. Their era spread the horse and [[e:chariot|chariot]] in [[e:egypt|Egypt]], and the Rhind Mathematical [[e:papyrus|Papyrus]] was copied under Apepi. Khyan's name appears on objects found as far as [[s:palace-state-of-knossos|Knossos]] and [[e:baghdad|Baghdad]].
fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.e: The [[s:seventeenth-dynasty-of-egypt|Seventeenth Dynasty of Egypt]] at [[s:thebes|Thebes]] went to war against Apepi. Around 1550 BCE [[e:ahmose-i|Ahmose I]] captured Avaris and then besieged Sharuhen in southern [[e:canaan|Canaan]], driving out the [[e:hyksos|Hyksos]] and founding the [[s:egyptian-empire-new-kingdom|Egyptian Empire New Kingdom]].

free-imperial-city-of-pfullendorf.t: Small Swabian imperial city north of Lake Constance, chartered by Frederick II in 1220 and a modest Catholic member of the Swabian city leagues.
free-imperial-city-of-pfullendorf.o: Pfullendorf was the seat of counts whose lands passed to the Hohenstaufen in the later 12th century. In 1220 Emperor [[e:frederick-ii|Frederick II]] granted the town its charter, and it became an imperial city on the roads between the [[e:danube|Danube]] and Lake Constance.
free-imperial-city-of-pfullendorf.r: The town was governed by a council with [[e:guild|guild]] participation and lived from linen weaving, crafts and its market for the surrounding countryside. Its small territory included a few villages. It joined the Swabian city leagues and later the Swabian imperial circle, but remained a minor power, and it stayed Catholic during the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]].
free-imperial-city-of-pfullendorf.e: Pfullendorf lost its imperial freedom in 1803 when it was annexed by the [[s:margraviate-of-baden|Margraviate of Baden]], soon the [[s:grand-duchy-of-baden|Grand Duchy of Baden]]. It is now a small town in Baden-Württemberg with a well-preserved old centre and parts of its medieval walls.

frentani.t: Oscan-speaking people of the central Adriatic coast, related to the Samnites, who became allies of Rome in 304 BCE.
frentani.o: The Frentani occupied the coastal hills of modern Molise and southern Abruzzo between the Sangro and the Fortore rivers. Ancient writers considered them of Samnite stock, and they spoke Oscan. Their history before [[e:rome|Rome]] is known only from scattered references.
frentani.r: Their main centres included Histonium (Vasto), Anxanum (Lanciano) and Larinum, which some writers treated as a separate people. They farmed, herded and traded along the coast. They usually kept apart from the [[s:samnite-league|Samnite League]] and its wars with [[e:rome|Rome]].
frentani.e: The Frentani made an alliance with [[e:rome|Rome]] in 304 BCE, at the end of the Second Samnite War, and fought for Rome against [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]]. They joined the Italian rebels in the Social War of 91–88 BCE, then received citizenship and were absorbed into Roman [[e:italy|Italy]].

first-portuguese-republic.t: Portugal's first republic, an era of anticlerical reform and chronic instability with some 45 governments in under 16 years.
first-portuguese-republic.o: After the assassination of King Carlos I in 1908, republican sentiment grew in [[e:lisbon|Lisbon]]. On 5 October 1910 a revolt by soldiers, sailors and Carbonária militants overthrew Manuel II, and a provisional government under Teófilo Braga proclaimed the republic, ending the [[s:kingdom-of-portugal|Kingdom of Portugal]].
first-portuguese-republic.r: The Constitution of 1911 created a parliamentary republic. Governments led by Afonso Costa separated Church and state, expelled the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]] and legalised divorce. Portugal entered the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] in 1916 and suffered heavy losses at La Lys in 1918. Strikes, coups, bombings and Sidónio Pais's brief dictatorship of 1917-1918 marked the period, along with the royalist [[s:monarchy-of-the-north|Monarchy of the North]].
first-portuguese-republic.e: On 28 May 1926 a military coup led by General Gomes da Costa overthrew the republic and set up the [[s:ditadura-nacional|Ditadura Nacional]].

first-mexican-empire.t: The short-lived empire of Agustín de Iturbide, the first independent Mexican state, which briefly stretched from California to Costa Rica.
first-mexican-empire.o: In February 1821 the royalist officer Agustín de Iturbide joined the insurgent Vicente Guerrero in the Plan of Iguala, promising independence, [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] and equality under a [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]]. The last Spanish [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]], Juan O'Donojú, accepted it in the Treaty of [[e:cordoba|Córdoba]] in August, and the Army of the Three Guarantees entered [[e:mexico-city|Mexico City]] on 27 September 1821.
first-mexican-empire.r: A regency governed while a European prince was sought, but none accepted, and in May 1822 crowds and soldiers acclaimed Iturbide as Emperor Agustín I. Central America joined the empire in January 1822. Iturbide clashed with the congress over money and power and dissolved it in October 1822. The treasury was empty, the army unpaid and the provinces restless.
first-mexican-empire.e: Antonio López de Santa Anna rose at Veracruz in December 1822, and the Plan of Casa Mata in 1823 won over the army. Iturbide abdicated in March 1823 and went into exile; on his return in 1824 he was executed. Central America broke away, and [[s:mexico|Mexico]] became the [[s:first-mexican-republic|First Mexican Republic]].

federal-republic-of-central-america.t: Federation of the five former provinces of the Kingdom of Guatemala, a liberal experiment that collapsed in civil war after less than two decades.
federal-republic-of-central-america.o: The provinces of the [[s:captaincy-general-of-guatemala|Captaincy General of Guatemala]] declared independence from [[e:spain|Spain]] in September 1821 and were absorbed into the [[s:first-mexican-empire|First Mexican Empire]] in 1822. After Iturbide's fall, a congress in [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]] City declared them independent on 1 July 1823 as the United Provinces of Central America, and a federal constitution followed in 1824.
federal-republic-of-central-america.r: [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]], [[s:republic-of-el-salvador|El Salvador]], [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]], [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]] and [[s:republic-of-costa-rica|Costa Rica]] each had their own governments under a weak federal president. Liberals and conservatives, and [[e:guatemala|Guatemala]] and its smaller neighbours, fought a civil war from 1826 to 1829. Francisco Morazán won and, as president from 1830, pursued anticlerical reforms, expelled religious orders and moved the capital to San [[e:salvador|Salvador]] in 1834. The federation was chronically short of revenue.
federal-republic-of-central-america.e: A rural revolt led by Rafael Carrera, fuelled by a cholera epidemic and resentment of liberal reforms, broke federal power in [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]]. [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]], [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]] and [[s:republic-of-costa-rica|Costa Rica]] seceded in 1838, and Morazán was defeated in 1840. The federation dissolved by 1841; Morazán was executed in Costa Rica in 1842.

free-imperial-city-of-donauworth.t: A Swabian imperial city on the Danube whose sectarian riot of 1606 and seizure by Bavaria helped set Europe on the road to the Thirty Years' War.
free-imperial-city-of-donauworth.o: Donauwörth grew where the Wörnitz meets the [[e:danube|Danube]], beside the Holy Cross abbey and a castle. A Hohenstaufen possession, it later fell under the dukes of Bavaria, from whom it repeatedly bought back its freedom. It counted as an imperial city from about 1301, although it was pledged to Bavaria again from 1376 until 1434.
free-imperial-city-of-donauworth.r: A council of [[e:burghers|burghers]] governed the town, which prospered from [[e:danube|Danube]] trade and the road between [[s:free-imperial-city-of-nuremberg|Nuremberg]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-augsburg|Augsburg]]. Most citizens became Lutheran, while the Benedictine Holy Cross abbey kept a Catholic minority. In 1606 Protestant townspeople attacked a Catholic procession, and the Imperial Aulic Council placed the city under the imperial ban.
free-imperial-city-of-donauworth.e: Duke Maximilian I of Bavaria executed the ban in 1607, occupied Donauwörth, re-Catholicised it and in 1609 annexed it. Alarmed Protestant princes formed the Protestant Union in 1608, and the [[e:catholic-league|Catholic League]] answered in 1609. Apart from a brief restoration of its imperial freedom from 1705 to 1714, the town has remained Bavarian ever since.

fourth-brazilian-republic.t: Brazil's democratic Populist Republic, the era of Petrobras and Brasília, which ended with the military coup of 1964.
fourth-brazilian-republic.o: After the fall of the [[s:estado-novo-brazil|Estado Novo (Brazil)]] in 1945, General Eurico Gaspar Dutra was elected president, and a new democratic constitution was adopted in 1946. It restored Congress, parties and elections, though illiterate people could not vote.
fourth-brazilian-republic.r: Getúlio Vargas returned as elected president in 1950 and founded Petrobras, the state oil company, in 1953. Facing a political crisis, he shot himself in 1954. Juscelino Kubitschek promised 'fifty years in five' and built the new capital, Brasília, inaugurated in 1960. Jânio Quadros resigned within months in 1961, and the military accepted his vice-president João Goulart only under a temporary parliamentary system.
fourth-brazilian-republic.e: Goulart's proposals for land reform and his ties to the left alarmed the military, the middle classes and the [[s:united-states|United States]]. A coup on 31 March and 1 April 1964 deposed him and began the [[s:brazilian-military-dictatorship|Brazilian military dictatorship]].

free-imperial-city-of-muhlhausen.t: Thuringian imperial city famous as the base of Thomas Müntzer during the Peasants' War and for one of the oldest law books written in German.
free-imperial-city-of-muhlhausen.o: Mühlhausen grew around a royal palace and was favoured by the Hohenstaufen emperors, gaining the status of an imperial city by about 1180. Around 1200 to 1230 its law was set down in the Mühlhausen Reichsrechtsbuch, one of the earliest legal texts in German.
free-imperial-city-of-muhlhausen.r: A council of patricians and later [[e:guild|guild]] representatives ruled the city, which grew rich from cloth, woad and trade, joined the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanseatic League]] and allied with Erfurt and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-nordhausen|Nordhausen]] in a Thuringian city league. In 1525 the radical preacher Thomas Müntzer made Mühlhausen his base, set up the Eternal League and led its men to defeat at Frankenhausen in the Peasants' War.
free-imperial-city-of-muhlhausen.e: After 1525 the city lost its freedom for two decades under [[e:saxons|Saxon]] and Hessian control, regaining imperial status in 1548. It was annexed by [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1802, belonged to the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]] from 1807 to 1813, and then returned to Prussia; it is now in Thuringia.

federation-of-malaya.t: Federation of Malay states and settlements that fought the communist Emergency and won independence from Britain in 1957.
federation-of-malaya.o: The Federation of [[e:malaya|Malaya]] replaced the [[s:malayan-union|Malayan Union]] on 1 February 1948, restoring the [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] of the nine Malay rulers and joining their states with [[s:prince-of-wales-island|Penang]] and [[e:malacca|Malacca]] under a British high commissioner. Months later the Malayan Communist Party launched an armed revolt, and the government declared the Malayan Emergency.
federation-of-malaya.r: Under the Briggs Plan and High Commissioner Gerald Templer, half a million rural Chinese were moved into new villages to cut off the [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrillas]]. The Alliance of UMNO, the Malayan Chinese Association and the Malayan Indian Congress won the 1955 election under Tunku Abdul Rahman, who negotiated independence on 31 August 1957. A rotating king, the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, was chosen from the rulers.
federation-of-malaya.e: The Emergency was declared over in 1960, though communist [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrillas]] remained on the Thai border. On 16 September 1963 the federation joined with [[s:singapore|Singapore]], Sabah and [[s:raj-of-sarawak|Sarawak]] to form [[s:malaysia|Malaysia]], which kept its constitution and institutions.

fidach.t: A Pictish province named in the legend of the seven sons of Cruithne, of uncertain location, perhaps around Moray and Ross.
fidach.o: Fidach is known only from medieval lists of the seven Pictish provinces, which named them after legendary sons of Cruithne, the father of the Picts. Its location is not stated, and historians have suggested [[s:kingdom-of-moray|Moray]], Ross or the area around the Moray Firth.
fidach.r: Nothing is known of its rulers, society or government beyond its inclusion in the province lists. It was presumably one of the regional territories of [[s:kingdom-of-the-picts|Pictland]], subject to the kings of the Picts.
fidach.e: Like the other provinces, it disappeared as a distinct unit when [[s:kingdom-of-the-picts|Pictland]] was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]] in the 9th and 10th centuries.

free-province-of-guayaquil.t: The independent port province of Guayaquil, freed in 1820, whose fate was settled when Bolívar annexed it on the eve of his meeting with San Martín.
free-province-of-guayaquil.o: On 9 October 1820 a group of patriots in Guayaquil, the main port of the [[s:royal-audiencia-of-quito|Royal Audiencia of Quito]], overthrew the Spanish authorities. A cabildo declared the Free Province of Guayaquil, with the poet José Joaquín de Olmedo as head of government.
free-province-of-guayaquil.r: The province adopted a provisional regulation of government and created an army, the Protective Division of Quito, to free the highlands. Its first campaigns failed, but with troops sent by Bolívar under Antonio José de Sucre, and Peruvian reinforcements, the patriots won at Pichincha in May 1822. Guayaquil's elite was divided over joining [[s:gran-colombia|Gran Colombia]], [[e:peru|Peru]] or staying independent.
free-province-of-guayaquil.e: Bolívar entered Guayaquil in July 1822 and annexed it to [[s:gran-colombia|Gran Colombia]]; Olmedo left in protest. Days later Bolívar met San Martín in the Guayaquil Conference. Guayaquil became part of the [[s:republic-of-ecuador|Republic of Ecuador]] in 1830.

free-imperial-city-of-turckheim.t: A walled Alsatian wine town, one of the smallest members of the Decapolis, near which Turenne won a decisive battle for France in 1675.
free-imperial-city-of-turckheim.o: Turckheim grew at the entrance to the Fecht valley near [[s:free-imperial-city-of-colmar|Colmar]], on lands long linked to the abbey of [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]]. Walled in the early 14th century, it was recognised as an imperial city around 1312 and in 1354 joined the [[s:decapolis|Decapolis]], the league of ten Alsatian imperial cities.
free-imperial-city-of-turckheim.r: A council of [[e:burghers|burghers]] ruled the town, whose wealth came almost wholly from its vineyards; its three gates and much of its wall survive. It remained Catholic during the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]]. The round of the night watchman, still re-enacted in summer, recalls the town's tradition of guarding its own walls.
free-imperial-city-of-turckheim.e: After 1648 the [[s:decapolis|Decapolis]] came under French protection. On 5 January 1675 Marshal [[s:viscounty-of-turenne|Turenne]] defeated the imperial army at the Battle of Turckheim, securing Alsace, and the Treaty of Nijmegen of 1679 confirmed annexation by the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]]. It is now in the Haut-Rhin [[e:departement|department]].

france-antarctique.t: A short-lived French colony in Guanabara Bay whose destruction by the Portuguese led directly to the founding of Rio de Janeiro.
france-antarctique.o: In 1555 the French admiral Nicolas Durand de Villegaignon, backed by Admiral Gaspard de Coligny, sailed to Guanabara Bay in [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] with some 600 settlers. They built Fort Coligny on a small island and allied with the Tupinambá, who traded [[e:brazilwood|brazilwood]] with French merchants.
france-antarctique.r: The colony was intended partly as a refuge for French Protestants, and a group of Calvinists sent from [[s:republic-of-geneva|Geneva]] arrived in 1557, including Jean de Léry, whose account of the Tupinambá became a classic of travel writing. Villegaignon, however, quarrelled with them over doctrine and expelled them, and some were executed. Harsh discipline and desertions weakened the settlement.
france-antarctique.e: Governor-general Mem de Sá destroyed Fort Coligny in 1560. His nephew Estácio de Sá founded [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]] in 1565 and, with Portuguese and Temiminó forces, drove the remaining French and their Tupinambá allies from the bay by 1567.

free-cities-of-menton-and-roquebrune.t: Two Riviera towns that broke away from Monaco in 1848 over taxes on their lemons and lived as free cities until France bought them.
free-cities-of-menton-and-roquebrune.o: Menton and Roquebrune formed most of the [[s:principality-of-monaco|Principality of Monaco]]'s territory and income, through their lemon and olive trade. Resentment at Prince Florestan I's taxes and monopolies boiled over in 1848, and in March the two towns declared themselves [[e:free-imperial-city|free cities]] under the protection of the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]].
free-cities-of-menton-and-roquebrune.r: The towns governed themselves through elected councils, with Sardinian troops present. A plebiscite favoured union with [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]], but it was never formally completed because of diplomatic objections. Their economy remained based on citrus fruit, and Menton began to attract winter visitors.
free-cities-of-menton-and-roquebrune.e: After [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]] ceded Nice to [[e:france|France]] in 1860, Menton and Roquebrune voted to join France. In 1861 Prince Charles III of [[s:principality-of-monaco|Monaco]] sold his rights to [[e:napoleon-iii|Napoleon III's]] [[s:second-french-empire|Second French Empire]] for four million francs.

free-imperial-city-of-esslingen.t: Wine town on the Neckar that was a leading Swabian imperial city, founding place of the Swabian League and a lasting rival of Württemberg.
free-imperial-city-of-esslingen.o: Esslingen grew around a shrine of Saint Vitalis and a bridge over the Neckar, gaining market rights in the Carolingian period. The Hohenstaufen favoured the town, and it was treated as an imperial city by the early 13th century, its privileges confirmed by [[e:frederick-ii|Frederick II]] around 1219.
free-imperial-city-of-esslingen.r: A council of patricians and [[e:guild|guilds]] governed the town, which prospered from wine, cloth and bridge tolls. Its position next to Württemberg led to repeated wars with the counts of Württemberg in the 14th and 15th centuries. In 1488 the Swabian League was founded at Esslingen, and the city hosted the imperial governing council in the 1520s. It adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in 1531.
free-imperial-city-of-esslingen.e: Esslingen lost its freedom in 1802 when it was annexed by Württemberg, its old enemy. It became an industrial town known for machine building and remains in Baden-Württemberg, with its Gothic churches and old town hall.

finnish-democratic-republic.t: Soviet puppet government created for Finland at the start of the Winter War, led by Otto Wille Kuusinen and abandoned in 1940.
finnish-democratic-republic.o: On 30 November 1939 the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] invaded [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]]. The next day it announced the formation of the Finnish Democratic Republic, nominally based in the border town of Terijoki, with the exiled Finnish communist Otto Wille Kuusinen as head. The [[e:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] recognised it as [[e:finland|Finland's]] only legitimate government and signed a treaty of mutual assistance with it.
finnish-democratic-republic.r: The 'Terijoki government' existed mainly on paper and was run from [[e:moscow|Moscow]]. It raised a Finnish People's Army from Soviet Finns and [[s:karelians|Karelians]], intended to enter Helsinki behind the Red Army. Finns overwhelmingly rejected it, and it helped unite Finnish society behind its real government.
finnish-democratic-republic.e: Finnish resistance forced the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] to negotiate with the Helsinki government. The [[e:moscow|Moscow]] Peace Treaty of March 1940 ended the war, and the puppet government was quietly dissolved. Its leaders and territory were merged into the new [[s:karelo-finnish-soviet-socialist-republic|Karelo-Finnish Soviet Socialist Republic]], with Kuusinen as its head.

free-france.t: Charles de Gaulle's government-in-exile and armed forces, which kept France in the war against Germany after 1940 and rallied much of the empire.
free-france.o: On 18 June 1940 General [[e:charles-de-gaulle|Charles de Gaulle]], refusing the [[e:armistice-of-11-november-1918|armistice]], broadcast from [[e:london|London]] on the BBC calling on the French to continue fighting. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] recognised him as leader of the Free French, and in August 1940 [[e:chad|Chad]], under its governor Félix Éboué, joined his cause, followed by most of [[s:french-equatorial-africa|French Equatorial Africa]].
free-france.r: Free [[e:france|France]] built an army and navy, fought at Bir Hakeim in 1942 and gathered colonies in [[e:africa|Africa]] and the Pacific. A French National Committee was set up in [[e:london|London]] in 1941. [[e:charles-de-gaulle|De Gaulle's]] envoy Jean Moulin united the internal Resistance in 1943. That year the movement moved to [[e:algiers|Algiers]] and merged with Henri Giraud's forces in the French Committee of National Liberation.
free-france.e: In June 1944 the committee became the [[s:provisional-government-of-the-french-republic|Provisional Government of the French Republic]], which returned to [[e:paris|Paris]] after its liberation in August 1944 and restored the Republic.

frisian-kingdom.t: Pagan kingdom of the North Sea coast, ruler of the trading port of Dorestad, which resisted the Franks for over a century.
frisian-kingdom.o: After the Roman period the coastal [[e:low-countries|Low Countries]] were resettled from the 5th century, and by around 600 the [[s:frisii|Frisians]] held a realm stretching along the coast from the Zwin to the Weser, later called Magna Frisia. Its first known king, Aldgisl, sheltered the English [[e:bishop|bishop]] Wilfrid in 678.
frisian-kingdom.r: The [[s:frisii|Frisians]] were seafaring traders whose merchants carried cloth, slaves and goods across the [[e:north-sea|North Sea]], and their emporium of Dorestad on the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] was one of the busiest ports in north-west [[e:europe|Europe]]. Their [[e:silver|silver]] sceattas circulated widely. King Redbad opposed the Christian mission of Willibrord.
frisian-kingdom.e: Pippin of Herstal defeated Redbad around 690 and took Dorestad and [[s:lordship-of-utrecht|Utrecht]], but Redbad recovered much ground before his death in 719. In 734 [[e:charles-martel|Charles Martel]] defeated and killed King Poppo at the Boarn, and Frisia was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-the-franks|Kingdom of the Franks]].

free-imperial-city-of-wangen.t: Small Catholic imperial city in the western Allgäu, a market for linen and scythes that kept its freedom until 1802.
free-imperial-city-of-wangen.o: Wangen grew around a settlement linked to the [[s:imperial-abbey-of-saint-gall|Imperial Abbey of Saint Gall]], which held rights there from the 9th century. The Hohenstaufen developed the town, and after their fall it was recognised as an imperial city by Rudolf I in 1286.
free-imperial-city-of-wangen.r: A council of [[e:burghers|burghers]] ruled the town and its small territory. Linen weaving, scythe making and the market for the western Allgäu were its main trades. Wangen remained Catholic during the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] and was a member of the Swabian imperial circle. It suffered heavily in the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years War]].
free-imperial-city-of-wangen.e: Wangen lost its freedom to Bavaria in 1802 and passed to Württemberg in 1810. It is now a town in Baden-Württemberg with a well-preserved old centre, gate towers and painted houses.

french-florida.t: A short-lived Huguenot colony on the St Johns River whose destruction by Spain in 1565 secured Florida for the Spanish crown.
french-florida.o: Backed by Admiral Gaspard de Coligny, the Protestant captain Jean Ribault sailed to Florida in 1562 and left a small garrison at Charlesfort, on Parris Island in modern South [[s:province-of-carolina|Carolina]], which was soon abandoned. In 1564 René Goulaine de Laudonnière brought a second expedition and built Fort Caroline near the mouth of the St Johns River.
french-florida.r: The colony was a fortified outpost of a few hundred soldiers, artisans and Huguenot settlers rather than a governed territory. It depended on food from the Timucua chief Saturiwa and his neighbours, and hunger and mutiny troubled it. The artist Jacques Le Moyne de Morgues drew the Timucua, leaving some of the earliest European images of [[e:north-america|North America]].
french-florida.e: In 1565 Philip II sent Pedro Menéndez de Avilés, who founded St Augustine, captured Fort Caroline and executed Ribault and his shipwrecked men at Matanzas Inlet. Dominique de Gourgues avenged them in 1568, but [[e:france|France]] did not return, leaving [[s:spanish-florida|Spanish Florida]] in control.

first-dominican-republic.t: The first Dominican republic, won from Haiti in 1844 and dominated by the rival strongmen Pedro Santana and Buenaventura Báez until its annexation by Spain.
first-dominican-republic.o: The [[e:secret-society|secret society]] La Trinitaria, founded in 1838 by Juan Pablo Duarte, organised resistance to Haitian rule. On 27 February 1844 Francisco del Rosario Sánchez and Ramón Matías Mella proclaimed independence at the Puerta del Conde in Santo Domingo. The [[e:cattle|cattle]] rancher Pedro Santana defeated the Haitian army and soon exiled Duarte and the other founders.
first-dominican-republic.r: The constitution of San Cristóbal of November 1844 included Article 210, giving Santana dictatorial powers. Santana and Buenaventura Báez alternated in power, each seeking foreign protection from [[e:france|France]], [[e:spain|Spain]] or the [[s:united-states|United States]]. The country repeatedly defended itself against Haitian invasions under Faustin Soulouque, notably at Las Carreras in 1849 and at Santomé and Sabana Larga in 1855 to 1856. Tobacco from the Cibao valley and mahogany were the main exports; [[e:printing-press|printing]] of [[e:paper-money|paper money]] caused ruinous [[e:inflation|inflation]].
first-dominican-republic.e: Fearing renewed Haitian attack and seeking to keep power, Santana negotiated the country's annexation to [[e:spain|Spain]], proclaimed on 18 March 1861, creating the [[s:province-of-santo-domingo-1861-1865|Province of Santo Domingo]].

federation-of-central-america-1921-1922.t: Short-lived union of Guatemala, El Salvador and Honduras proclaimed for the centenary of independence in 1921, which fell apart within months.
federation-of-central-america-1921-1922.o: For the hundredth anniversary of independence, delegates of the five Central American states signed a Pact of Union at San José in January 1921. [[s:republic-of-costa-rica|Costa Rica]] did not ratify it and [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]] withdrew, but [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]], [[s:republic-of-el-salvador|El Salvador]] and [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]] went ahead, and a constituent assembly in Tegucigalpa adopted a federal constitution in September 1921.
federation-of-central-america-1921-1922.r: The constitution provided for a federal council, congress and courts, with the member states keeping control of most domestic affairs. A provisional federal council met in Tegucigalpa while institutions were set up, but the new federation had little money or authority, and member governments were wary of surrendering power.
federation-of-central-america-1921-1922.e: In December 1921 a coup in [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]] brought General José María Orellana to power, and in January 1922 he withdrew [[e:guatemala|Guatemala]] from the federation. [[s:republic-of-el-salvador|El Salvador]] and [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]] followed, and the federation dissolved in early 1922. It was the last formal attempt at Central American political union.

free-state-of-oldenburg.t: North-west German republic that succeeded the grand duchy and in 1932 elected one of the first Nazi state governments.
free-state-of-oldenburg.o: Grand Duke Frederick [[e:augustus-ii-the-strong|Augustus II]] abdicated in November 1918, and [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] became a free state, with a constitution adopted in 1919. It kept the detached principalities of [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck|Lübeck]] around Eutin and Birkenfeld in the Hunsrück.
free-state-of-oldenburg.r: [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] was rural, with dairy farming in the marshes and moors and a naval port at Wilhelmshaven nearby. Its Lutheran north and Catholic south around Cloppenburg and Vechta differed politically. In 1932 the Nazis won an absolute majority, and Carl Röver formed one of the first Nazi state governments. In 1937 the Greater [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-hamburg|Hamburg]] Act transferred [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck|Lübeck]] and Birkenfeld to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and gave Wilhelmshaven to Oldenburg.
free-state-of-oldenburg.e: Under the Nazis, Röver became Reich governor for [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] and [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]]. After 1945 the state lay in the British zone, and in November 1946 it was merged with Hanover, Brunswick and [[s:principality-of-schaumburg-lippe|Schaumburg-Lippe]] into the state of Lower Saxony. Oldenburg survives as a historic region and administrative name.

free-imperial-city-of-dinkelsbuhl.t: A walled imperial city on the Wörnitz whose intact medieval fortifications make it one of Germany's best-preserved old towns.
free-imperial-city-of-dinkelsbuhl.o: Dinkelsbühl grew at a crossing of trade routes on the Wörnitz and received town rights under the Hohenstaufen. After being pledged by the crown to various lords, it secured its status as a free imperial city in 1351, when [[e:charles-iv|Charles IV]] promised that it would not be pledged again.
free-imperial-city-of-dinkelsbuhl.r: In 1387 the [[e:guild|guilds]] won a share of power in the council. Cloth, scythe-making and trade brought prosperity, visible in the late Gothic church of Saint George. The town became mixed in religion, and the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] made it one of four imperial cities where Catholics and Lutherans shared council offices equally.
free-imperial-city-of-dinkelsbuhl.e: Swedish troops occupied the town in the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years' War]], but it escaped destruction; local tradition says its children persuaded the Swedish colonel to spare it, a story celebrated in the Kinderzeche festival. In 1802 it passed to Bavaria, was Prussian from 1804 to 1806 and then returned to Bavaria. Its walls, gates and houses survive almost intact.

frankish-kingdom-of-soissons.t: Merovingian kingdom of Chlothar I, who from his base at Soissons gradually reunited all the Frankish lands.
frankish-kingdom-of-soissons.o: When [[e:clovis-i|Clovis]] died in 511, his youngest son Chlothar I received the old Frankish heartland in the north, between the [[e:battle-of-the-somme|Somme]] and the Scheldt, ruling from Soissons, the former seat of the [[s:domain-of-soissons|Domain of Soissons]].
frankish-kingdom-of-soissons.r: Chlothar was the most ruthless of [[e:clovis-i|Clovis]]' sons. In 524 he personally killed two of his young nephews to seize part of the [[s:kingdom-of-orleans|Kingdom of Orléans]]. He shared in the conquest of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-burgundians|Kingdom of the Burgundians]] and of Thuringia, where he took the princess Radegund as his wife.
frankish-kingdom-of-soissons.e: Through the deaths of his brothers and nephew, Chlothar inherited [[s:austrasia|Austrasia]] in 555 and [[e:paris|Paris]] in 558, reuniting the [[s:kingdom-of-the-franks|Kingdom of the Franks]]. He died in 561 and was buried at Saint-Médard in Soissons. His son Chilperic I received Soissons, the core of [[s:neustria|Neustria]].

free-city-of-krakow.t: A small city republic around Krakow under the joint protection of Austria, Prussia and Russia, the last free remnant of Poland.
free-city-of-krakow.o: Unable to agree who should have Krakow, the powers at the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] in 1815 made the city and its surrounding district a free, independent and strictly neutral city under the protection of [[e:austria|Austria]], [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and [[e:russia|Russia]].
free-city-of-krakow.r: Krakow had a senate, an assembly and its own constitution, though the three protecting powers supervised it through their residents. It was the only place where Polish institutions functioned freely, and the Jagiellonian University was a centre of Polish culture. Its free-trade status helped commerce, and it became a refuge for Polish patriots and conspirators.
free-city-of-krakow.e: In February 1846 a national uprising broke out in Krakow and quickly collapsed. In November 1846 [[e:austria|Austria]] annexed the city with the agreement of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and [[e:russia|Russia]], joining it to the [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria]] as the Grand [[s:duchy-of-krakow|Duchy of Krakow]].

first-toungoo-empire.t: The largest empire in the history of Southeast Asia, built by Tabinshwehti and Bayinnaung, which briefly ruled from Manipur to Laos and Ayutthaya.
first-toungoo-empire.o: Toungoo, a small Burmese principality on the Sittaung river, grew in strength under Mingyi Nyo, who declared independence from Ava in 1510. His son Tabinshwehti, from 1530, conquered the [[s:hanthawaddy-kingdom|Hanthawaddy Kingdom]], made Pegu his capital in 1539 and seized [[s:prome-kingdom|Prome]] and much of central [[s:myanmar|Myanmar]].
first-toungoo-empire.r: Bayinnaung, king from 1550, took Ava in 1555, subdued the Shan states and [[s:kingdom-of-manipur|Manipur]], conquered [[s:lan-na|Lan Na]] in 1558 and [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]] in 1564 and 1569, and campaigned in [[s:lan-xang|Lan Xang]]. He governed through [[e:vassal|vassal]] rulers bound by oaths and hostages, standardised weights and law, and patronised [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]]. Pegu was a wealthy port visited by Portuguese and Venetian traders.
first-toungoo-empire.e: After Bayinnaung's death in 1581 the empire fell apart; Naresuan freed [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]] in 1584, and Nanda Bayin's wars exhausted the realm. Pegu was sacked by [[s:mrauk-u-kingdom|Arakan]] and Toungoo in 1599. Nyaungyan Min rebuilt the state as the [[s:restored-toungoo-kingdom|Restored Toungoo Kingdom]].

free-imperial-city-of-biberach.t: Upper Swabian imperial city of fustian weavers, shared after 1648 by Catholics and Protestants, where the writer Wieland served as town clerk.
free-imperial-city-of-biberach.o: Biberach grew as a market town on the Riss under the Hohenstaufen, at the crossing of roads in Upper Swabia. After their fall, it was recognised as an imperial city by Rudolf I around 1282, on the road from Ulm to Lake Constance.
free-imperial-city-of-biberach.r: A council of patricians and [[e:guild|guilds]] governed. Fustian weaving and the linen trade made Biberach prosperous in the 15th and 16th centuries. The city adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]], but after the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years War]] it became a parity city in which Catholics and Lutherans shared every office and even the parish church. Christoph Martin Wieland, born nearby, served as its town clerk from 1760 to 1769.
free-imperial-city-of-biberach.e: Biberach lost its freedom in 1802 to Baden and was transferred to Württemberg in 1806. It is now a town in Baden-Württemberg, where a museum and an annual festival recall its parity tradition and Wieland.

free-imperial-city-of-landau.t: A Palatinate wine town that held imperial-city status for four centuries before Louis XIV annexed it and made it a fortress.
free-imperial-city-of-landau.o: Founded by the counts of [[s:principality-of-leiningen|Leiningen]] around 1260, Landau received town rights from King Rudolf I in 1274, and in 1291 King Rudolf I granted it the privileges of a free imperial city. In the 1320s Louis the Bavarian pledged the town to the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-speyer|Speyer]], and Landau had to buy back its freedom, which it achieved only in 1511.
free-imperial-city-of-landau.r: A walled market town in the vineyards of the southern [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]], Landau was governed by a council and lived from wine, crafts and trade. From 1521 it belonged to the [[s:decapolis|Decapolis]], the league of Alsatian imperial cities, and it accepted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in the 16th century. Its position made it a target in every war along the upper [[e:rhine|Rhine]].
free-imperial-city-of-landau.e: The [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 placed the [[s:decapolis|Decapolis]] under French protection, and in 1680 [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV's]] Chambers of [[s:ile-bourbon|Reunion]] annexed Landau outright; Vauban rebuilt it as a great fortress. It passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]] in 1816 and is now Landau in der Pfalz in [[e:germany|Germany]].

first-east-turkestan-republic.t: A short-lived Islamic republic proclaimed at Kashgar in 1933 during the rebellions in Xinjiang, the first attempt at an independent Uyghur state.
first-east-turkestan-republic.o: The abolition of the [[s:kumul-khanate|Kumul Khanate]] in 1930 provoked revolts across [[e:xinjiang|Xinjiang]] against Governor Jin Shuren. In the south, rebels from [[s:kingdom-of-khotan|Khotan]] led by Muhammad Amin Bughra and the cleric Sabit Damulla took [[s:kingdom-of-shule|Kashgar]], and on 12 November 1933 proclaimed the Turkish Islamic Republic of East Turkestan.
first-east-turkestan-republic.r: The republic was based on Islamic law and Turkic nationalism, with Sabit Damulla as prime minister and the Kumul rebel leader Khoja Niyaz named president, though he never ruled from [[s:kingdom-of-shule|Kashgar]]. It had a constitution, flag and coins but little control beyond the southern oases, and it failed to win recognition from the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] or [[s:islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-present|Afghanistan]].
first-east-turkestan-republic.e: In early 1934 Hui Muslim troops of Ma Zhongying, retreating from the north, took [[s:kingdom-of-shule|Kashgar]] and crushed the republic. Khoja Niyaz came to terms with the new governor Sheng Shicai and handed Sabit Damulla over. The idea revived in the [[s:second-east-turkestan-republic|Second East Turkestan Republic]].

free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen.t: Weser port and Hanseatic city that won self-government in the Middle Ages and survives today as Germany's smallest federal state.
free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen.o: [[e:bremen|Bremen]] grew as the seat of the archbishops of Hamburg-Bremen. In 1186 [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] granted its citizens rights that freed them from many of the archbishop's claims. Joining the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanseatic League]] in the 13th century, the city slowly won self-government from the [[s:prince-archbishopric-of-bremen|Prince-Archbishopric of Bremen]], symbolised by the Roland statue of 1404.
free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen.r: A council of merchant families governed from the Gothic town hall, and wealth came from the Weser trade in grain, beer, [[e:timber|timber]] and later tobacco and [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]]. [[e:bremen|Bremen]] adopted the Reformed Protestant faith in the late 16th century. Its status as a free imperial city was confirmed by the Linz Diploma of 1646, protecting it against Swedish claims after 1648.
free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen.e: [[e:bremen|Bremen]] kept its freedom in 1803, was annexed by Napoleonic [[e:france|France]] from 1810 to 1813, and joined the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]] and [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] as a city-state. Mayor Johann Smidt founded Bremerhaven in 1827. Since 1949 the Free Hanseatic City of Bremen has been a federal state of [[e:germany|Germany]].

french-polynesia.t: France's Pacific overseas collectivity of 118 islands around Tahiti, shaped by three decades of nuclear testing and a long debate over autonomy and independence.
french-polynesia.o: In 1946 the [[s:french-establishments-in-oceania|French Establishments in Oceania]] became an overseas territory of the [[s:french-fourth-republic|French Union]], and in 1957 it was renamed French Polynesia. The nationalist leader Pouvanaa a Oopa, who campaigned for independence, was exiled in 1958 after a disputed conviction.
french-polynesia.r: From 1966 to 1996 [[e:france|France]] carried out 193 nuclear tests at Moruroa and Fangataufa atolls, first in the atmosphere and later underground, bringing money and jobs but lasting health and environmental harm. The resumption of testing in 1995 caused riots in Papeete. Statutes of 1984, 1996 and 2004 extended autonomy, and politics was long a contest between Gaston Flosse, favouring ties to France, and the pro-independence Oscar Temaru.
french-polynesia.e: French Polynesia is an overseas collectivity with its own president and assembly. The [[e:united-nations|United Nations]] relisted it as a non-self-governing territory in 2013. Tourism and black pearls are the main earners alongside French [[e:subsidy|subsidies]].

french-protectorate-in-morocco.t: French rule over most of Morocco from 1912, shaped by Lyautey's modern cities and ended by a nationalist movement led by the sultan himself.
french-protectorate-in-morocco.o: After the Agadir crisis, [[e:france|France]] forced [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Abd al-Hafid of the [[s:alaouite-sultanate|Alaouite Sultanate]] to sign the Treaty of [[e:fez|Fez]] in March 1912, establishing a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]]. Hubert Lyautey, the first resident-general, made [[e:rabat|Rabat]] the capital and spent years subduing the [[e:atlas-mountains|Atlas]] tribes.
french-protectorate-in-morocco.r: The sultan and makhzen remained in place, but the resident-general governed. Lyautey built new European cities beside the old medinas and developed Casablanca's port. French settlers took fertile land, and phosphate mining grew. The [[e:berbers|Berber]] Dahir of 1930 sparked nationalist protest, and the Istiqlal party demanded independence in 1944.
french-protectorate-in-morocco.e: [[e:france|France]] deposed and exiled [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Mohammed V in 1953, provoking violent unrest. He returned in 1955, and France recognised Moroccan independence in March 1956. Mohammed V adopted the title of king, forming the [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Kingdom of Morocco]].

free-state-of-lippe.t: Small Westphalian republic whose January 1933 election the Nazis used as a showcase just before Hitler came to power.
free-state-of-lippe.o: Prince Leopold IV abdicated on 12 November 1918, and Lippe became a free state with Detmold as capital. A constitution adopted in 1920 established a parliamentary government with a small Landtag.
free-state-of-lippe.r: Lippe was rural, with small farms, furniture making and a tradition of seasonal brickmakers. Social Democrats and liberals generally governed. In the Landtag election of 15 January 1933 the Nazis concentrated their campaign on the tiny state, with Hitler speaking repeatedly, and their gain of votes was presented as proof of momentum two weeks before he became chancellor. Under the Nazis Lippe shared a Reich governor with [[s:principality-of-schaumburg-lippe|Schaumburg-Lippe]], Alfred Meyer.
free-state-of-lippe.e: After 1945 Lippe was in the British zone. Rather than joining Lower Saxony, it opted in January 1947 to join North Rhine-[[e:peace-of-westphalia|Westphalia]], under guarantees known as the Lippe Punctations.

falkland-islands.t: A British territory in the South Atlantic, settled by sheep farmers and claimed by Argentina as the Malvinas, which went to war over it in 1982.
falkland-islands.o: [[e:france|France]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:spain|Spain]] had established rival settlements in the islands in the 18th century. In the 1820s the [[s:united-provinces-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|United Provinces of the Río de la Plata]] appointed Louis Vernet as governor. In January 1833 a British warship expelled the Argentine garrison, and [[e:britain|Britain]] took control. A crown colony was formed in 1841, and Stanley became the capital in 1845.
falkland-islands.r: The islands developed as a sheep-farming colony, much of it owned by the Falkland Islands Company, with a small population of British descent. Port Stanley served ships rounding Cape Horn. [[s:argentine-republic|Argentina]] maintained its claim. On 2 April 1982 [[e:argentina|Argentina's]] military government invaded; a British task force retook the islands, and Argentina surrendered on 14 June after a war that killed over 900 people.
falkland-islands.e: Fishing licences from 1987 transformed the economy. In a 2013 referendum over 99 per cent of voters chose to stay British. The islands remain a British Overseas Territory, and [[s:argentine-republic|Argentina]] still claims them.

federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south.t: The British-sponsored union of protected states in the Aden hinterland, created in 1959 to secure Britain's base at Aden.
federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south.o: Facing Arab nationalism and claims by the [[s:mutawakkilite-kingdom-of-yemen|Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] encouraged the rulers of the [[s:aden-protectorate|Western Aden Protectorate]] to federate. On 11 February 1959 six states, the [[s:audhali-sultanate|Audhali Sultanate]], [[s:emirate-of-beihan|Emirate of Beihan]], [[s:emirate-of-dhala|Emirate of Dhala]], [[s:fadhli-sultanate|Fadhli Sultanate]], [[s:lower-yafa-sultanate|Lower Yafa Sultanate]] and [[s:upper-aulaqi-sheikhdom|Upper Aulaqi Sheikhdom]], signed the federation treaty with [[e:britain|Britain]].
federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south.r: The federation had a supreme council of rulers and a federal government at Al Ittihad, a new capital built near Aden. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] kept responsibility for defence and foreign affairs and provided aid and the Federal Regular Army. Other states, including the [[s:sultanate-of-lahej|Sultanate of Lahej]], joined in the following years.
federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south.e: In April 1962 the federation was renamed the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]], in preparation for the entry of the [[s:colony-of-aden|Colony of Aden]] in 1963.

federal-state-of-the-visayas.t: Revolutionary government of the central Philippines, based in Iloilo, which took over from Spain at the end of 1898.
federal-state-of-the-visayas.o: As the revolution spread to the Visayan islands in 1898, local leaders in Panay organised a cantonal government in Iloilo, inspired by federalist ideas. Revolutionary forces under General Martin Delgado besieged Iloilo, and on 25 December 1898 the Spanish garrison surrendered, leaving the Federal State of the Visayas in control.
federal-state-of-the-visayas.r: The federal state was headed by Roque Lopez as president, with a council representing islands such as Panay and Negros, and it acknowledged the authority of Emilio Aguinaldo. Its leaders came from the wealthy [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]]-producing and merchant families of Iloilo. It lasted only weeks as an effective government.
federal-state-of-the-visayas.e: American troops took Iloilo on 11 February 1899 at the start of the Philippine-American War. The federal government was merged into the [[s:first-philippine-republic|First Philippine Republic]], and resistance on Panay continued until 1901.

french-algeria.t: France's largest settler colony, conquered from 1830 and governed as part of France, whose end in 1962 came after one of the bloodiest wars of decolonisation.
french-algeria.o: [[e:france|France]] invaded the [[s:regency-of-algiers|Regency of Algiers]] in 1830 after a diplomatic incident. Conquest of the interior took decades of brutal war, notably against the [[s:emirate-of-abdelkader|Emirate of Abdelkader]], defeated in 1847 by forces led by Thomas-Robert Bugeaud, and against Kabylia and the 1871 [[s:kingdom-of-ait-abbas|Mokrani]] revolt.
french-algeria.r: In 1848 northern [[e:algeria|Algeria]] was divided into French [[e:departement|departments]]. European settlers, later called [[e:pieds-noirs|pieds-noirs]], received land seized from Algerians and held political power, while Muslims were subjects under the Code de l'[[e:indigenat|indigénat]] without full citizenship. The Crémieux Decree of 1870 granted citizenship to Algerian [[e:jews|Jews]]. Wine, grain and citrus were key exports.
french-algeria.e: The Sétif massacres of 1945 hardened nationalism, and the FLN launched the war of independence in 1954. After hundreds of thousands of deaths, the [[e:evian-accords|Évian Accords]] of 1962 under de Gaulle led to independence that July, and most settlers left for [[e:france|France]].

free-imperial-city-of-worms.t: Ancient Rhine city of the Nibelungenlied, the Concordat of 1122 and Luther's defiance at the Diet of 1521, home of one of Europe's oldest Jewish communities.
free-imperial-city-of-worms.o: Worms was a Roman and Frankish centre, seat of a [[e:bishop|bishop]] and in legend of the Burgundian kings of the Nibelungenlied. Its citizens won growing privileges from the Salian emperors, who signed the Concordat of Worms there in 1122. [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa's]] charter of 1184 confirmed the city's freedoms, and it gradually threw off the bishop's lordship.
free-imperial-city-of-worms.r: A council of [[e:burghers|burghers]] ruled, frequently in conflict with the [[e:bishop|bishop]]. Worms hosted many [[e:imperial-diet|imperial diets]], most famously in 1521, when Martin Luther refused to recant before [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]]. Its Jewish community, with [[s:free-imperial-city-of-speyer|Speyer]] and [[e:mainz|Mainz]] one of the SchUM centres of [[e:ashkenazi-jews|Ashkenazi]] learning, had a synagogue and cemetery dating from the 11th century. The city adopted [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]].
free-imperial-city-of-worms.e: French troops burned Worms in 1689, and it never fully recovered. Revolutionary [[e:france|France]] annexed it in 1797. In 1816 it passed to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Grand Duchy of Hesse]], and it is now in Rhineland-Palatinate, where the SchUM sites are a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland.t: A British-created union of Southern Rhodesia, Northern Rhodesia and Nyasaland, rejected by African nationalists and dissolved after ten years.
federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland.o: White settler leaders, chiefly Godfrey Huggins of [[s:southern-rhodesia|Southern Rhodesia]] and Roy Welensky of [[s:northern-rhodesia|Northern Rhodesia]], pressed for a union of the three British territories in central [[e:africa|Africa]]. Despite African opposition, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] created the Federation of [[s:rhodesia|Rhodesia]] and [[s:nyasaland|Nyasaland]], or Central African Federation, in 1953, with its capital at Salisbury.
federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland.r: A federal government handled defence, economy and railways, while the territories kept their own governments. The federation promised racial 'partnership', but voting rights remained mostly white. [[e:copper|Copper]] revenues financed growth and the Kariba Dam on the [[e:zambezi|Zambezi]], mainly benefiting [[s:southern-rhodesia|Southern Rhodesia]]. The 1959 emergency in [[s:nyasaland|Nyasaland]] and the Devlin and Monckton reports undermined its legitimacy.
federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] allowed [[s:nyasaland|Nyasaland]] and [[s:northern-rhodesia|Northern Rhodesia]] to leave, and the federation was dissolved on 31 December 1963. Malawi and [[e:zambia|Zambia]] became independent in 1964, while [[s:southern-rhodesia|Southern Rhodesia]] moved towards unilateral independence.
